name: Biryani (Bhopali Style)
instructions: 1. Marinate mutton with curd, ginger-garlic paste, red chili, turmeric, salt, and half the fried onions for 2 hours.
2. Boil rice with whole spices until 70% cooked and drain.
3. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot (handi), fry potatoes until golden, and set aside.
4. In the same pot, cook the marinated mutton until half-done.
5. Layer the par-boiled rice over the mutton and potatoes.
6. Sprinkle saffron milk, fresh coriander, mint, and remaining fried onions on top.
7. Cover tightly (dum) and cook on low heat for 20-30 minutes until the meat is tender and rice is fluffy.
description: Bhopali Biryani is a quintessential part of Madhya Pradesh's culinary heritage, reflecting the city's rich Nawabi history. Unlike Hyderabadi variations, it often features potatoes and a unique balance of aromatic spices, symbolizing the fusion of North Indian and Deccan cooking traditions prevalent in Bhopal.
